blocks.instruction: Leia o texto e escolha a alternativa correta. Algumas perguntas pedem inferência — a resposta não está escrita com todas as letras.
blocks.passage:
At enterprise scale, transportation strategy is no longer about choosing between road and sea for a specific shipment. It is about building a portfolio of lanes, modes and carriers that together give the company the right balance of cost, service and resilience across a thousand simultaneous movements. The portfolio has to work on a normal week, a peak week and a bad week — because all three happen every year.

The strategic questions are few but demanding. Which lanes are so core to us that we should own them — fleet, drivers, dedicated routes — rather than rent them? Which lanes are so variable that multi-carrier flexibility is worth the small premium it costs? Which modes should we deliberately stop using, because they no longer fit the shape of our customers?

The best transportation strategies I have seen are uncomfortable documents. They accept explicit trade-offs instead of pretending that one portfolio can deliver cheapest, fastest and most resilient at the same time. That acceptance, at the top, is what makes the whole operation calmer further down.

items.q: According to the text, at enterprise scale transportation strategy is primarily about…
options: standardising on a single preferred carrier
choosing road or sea for a specific shipment
minimising cost on the busiest lane
building a portfolio of lanes, modes and carriers
items.why: "It is about building a portfolio of lanes, modes and carriers…" — a escala muda a natureza da decisão.

items.q: Why must the portfolio work on "a normal week, a peak week and a bad week"?
options: Because all three occur every year
Because regulators audit each type of week
Because bad weeks never actually happen
Because peak weeks are the cheapest to serve
items.why: "because all three happen every year" — o portfólio precisa aguentar os três cenários.

items.q: The author describes the best transportation strategies as "uncomfortable documents". This suggests that…
options: they are badly written and hard to follow
they are kept confidential from most of the company
they are rejected by senior leadership
they honestly name trade-offs rather than promising everything at once
items.why: Inferência: são desconfortáveis porque assumem trade-offs explícitos em vez de prometer tudo ao mesmo tempo.

items.q: Which statement would the author most likely DISAGREE with?
options: A single portfolio can be cheapest, fastest and most resilient simultaneously
Some modes should be dropped when they no longer fit customers
Multi-carrier flexibility can be worth a small premium
Owning some lanes can be justified when they are core to the business
items.why: Inferência: o texto rejeita explicitamente a ideia de que um só portfólio entrega tudo ao mesmo tempo.

items.q: The final sentence implies that clarity about trade-offs at the top…
options: increases the number of carriers required
makes little difference to daily operations
reduces panic and instability lower down in the operation
is mainly a matter of documentation
items.why: Inferência: "makes the whole operation calmer further down" — aceitar os trade-offs em cima estabiliza a base.

blocks.instruction: Ouça Oliver apresentando o documento de estratégia à liderança. Responda sem ler a transcrição — ela só aparece depois de corrigir.

audio.text:
Thank you all for making the time. What I'm putting in front of you today is not a tidy document, and I'd ask you to resist the urge to make it tidy. It ends three legacy contracts we've clung to out of habit, it doubles our investment in the north-south corridor, and — this is the part that will make some of you uneasy — it deliberately accepts a slightly higher unit cost on that corridor.

Let me be blunt about why. Those three legacy lanes look cheap on a spreadsheet, but every peak week they fail us, and we pay for that failure in expedites, in penalties, and in the calls I take at two in the morning. The higher unit cost on the core corridor is not waste. It is the price of owning capacity that is actually there when the week turns bad.

I am not asking you to believe that this portfolio is cheapest. It isn't, and I won't pretend otherwise. I'm asking you to accept, out loud, that we are buying resilience with that premium. If we can make that trade-off here, in this room, the whole operation below us gets a great deal calmer.
audio.label: Ouça quantas vezes precisar. A transcrição aparece depois de corrigir.

items.q: What are the three main things Oliver's document does?
options: Merges three lanes, renegotiates penalties, and freezes investment
Renews three contracts, opens a new corridor, and cuts unit cost
Ends three legacy contracts, doubles investment in a corridor, and accepts a higher unit cost there
Adds three carriers, cuts headcount, and lowers unit cost
items.why: "It ends three legacy contracts… doubles our investment in the north-south corridor… deliberately accepts a slightly higher unit cost."

items.q: Why does Oliver say the three legacy lanes are a problem despite looking cheap?
options: They fail every peak week, creating expedites and penalties
They are operated by a single carrier
They cover routes the company no longer serves
They require too many drivers
items.why: "every peak week they fail us, and we pay for that failure in expedites, in penalties…"

items.q: When Oliver says the higher unit cost "is not waste", he means it is…
options: a penalty imposed by the carriers
the price of owning capacity that holds up in a bad week
an error he will correct later
a temporary accounting adjustment
items.why: "It is the price of owning capacity that is actually there when the week turns bad."

items.q: What is Oliver really asking the leadership to do?
options: Consciously accept that they are buying resilience with a premium
Delegate the trade-off to the operations team
Delay the decision until costs fall
Approve the cheapest possible portfolio
items.why: Inferência: ele não pede que acreditem que é o mais barato — pede que aceitem, em voz alta, comprar resiliência com o prêmio.

items.q: How would you best describe Oliver's tone?
options: Candid and deliberately uncomfortable, but confident in the trade-off
Apologetic about the whole strategy
Detached and purely procedural
Evasive and reluctant to give figures
items.why: Inferência: ele é franco ("let me be blunt"), assume o desconforto, mas defende a lógica com segurança.

blocks.instruction: O vocabulário da lição aparece aqui em frases novas. Escolha o sentido ou a palavra que cabe no contexto.

items.q: "We manage a portfolio of lanes, not a single route." A portfolio here is…
options: a diversified set of options managed together
a legal contract with one carrier
a physical folder of shipping documents
the busiest lane in the network
items.why: Portfolio = portfólio: um conjunto diversificado gerido em bloco, não uma única opção.

items.q: Choose the correct word: "Because demand on that route is so ___, we keep it on multi-carrier terms rather than a fixed contract."
options: simultaneous
dedicated
core
variable
items.why: Variable = variável: demanda instável pede flexibilidade de vários transportadores.

items.q: "The corridor carries a small premium." In this context, a premium is…
options: a penalty for late delivery
a discount for high volume
a reward given to the best carrier
an extra amount paid above the baseline cost
items.why: Premium = prêmio/ágio: o valor a mais que se paga acima do custo base.

items.q: Choose the correct term: "A ___ of company-owned trucks gives us control that rented capacity cannot."
options: peak week
lane
fleet
trade-off
items.why: Fleet = frota: o conjunto de veículos próprios da empresa.

items.q: "Every design forces a trade-off." A trade-off is…
options: a compromise where gaining one thing costs another
a guaranteed win with no downside
a negotiation over price only
an exchange of trade documents
items.why: Trade-off = compromisso: ganhar em uma dimensão implica ceder em outra.

blocks.instruction: Expressões que aparecem em reuniões de estratégia logística. Escolha o sentido no contexto.

items.q: "The board still has to sign off on the new transportation strategy." To sign off on means to…
options: formally approve
postpone indefinitely
announce to the press
comment informally
items.why: Sign off on = aprovar formalmente, dar o aval final.

items.q: "We'll roll out the new lane structure corridor by corridor." To roll out means to…
options: implement it in stages
present it to the board
cancel it in phases
keep it under review
items.why: Roll out = implementar de forma progressiva, por etapas.

items.q: "Two regional heads pushed back on the higher unit cost." They…
options: approved it at once
ignored the proposal
rewrote the whole document
resisted or challenged it
items.why: Push back on = resistir, contestar — sem necessariamente rejeitar de vez.

items.q: "We agreed to drop the legacy lanes but never followed through." They…
options: failed to carry it to completion
documented it in detail
delegated it successfully
carried it out completely
items.why: Follow through = levar até o fim o que foi combinado — aqui, não foi levado.

items.q: "Shaving cents off a failing lane won't move the needle on resilience." This means it will…
options: require board approval
raise costs sharply
solve the problem overnight
not make a noticeable difference
items.why: Move the needle = mexer o ponteiro, fazer diferença perceptível — aqui, não faz.
